Common Questions Quick answers about Palma.ai's enterprise MCP platform What is Palma.ai in one sentence? Palma.ai is the enterprise governance layer for MCP — it gives every person and agent a single governed connector carrying the tools and Skills they're entitled to, enforces policies on the actual arguments of a call, pauses high-risk actions for approval, and records everything in a tamper-evident audit trail. What does MCP governance mean? Deciding which person may use which tool, with which arguments, with whose approval — and being able to prove it afterwards. MCP itself covers how a client authenticates to a server and how a tool is described and called; it does not decide which person may use which tool, hold a risky call for a human, or keep the record an auditor asks for. Palma adds that layer: one governed connector per person, assigned by identity-provider group, carrying the tools and Skills they are entitled to into whichever assistant they already use. Does my team have to set up MCP servers themselves? No. Connectors are assigned by IdP group through Entra or Okta, so a joiner gets theirs on day one and a leaver loses it the moment the group changes. Every MCP server your team approves arrives through that same connector — no per-user install, no config files, no credentials sitting on a laptop. What's a Skill, and why does it matter? A tool is a verb — "send an email". A Skill is the playbook that tells an agent when and how to use the verbs it already has: how your team actually closes the books, runs an incident review, or qualifies a lead. Skills are versioned, scanned before they're served, and scoped like any other piece of enterprise software — so your best operator's process reaches everyone else's agent. Does it work with the AI clients we already use? Yes — everything is served over MCP, so the same connector, Skills and policies follow the person into whichever assistant they open, whether that's Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor or something else. Switching tools doesn't mean re-approving, re-installing or re-auditing anything. How do we prove what an agent actually did? Every tool call is attributed to the person it was done for, the agent that did it, and the application it ran in — with the arguments, result, duration and cost. The audit trail is tamper-evident and verifiable offline with your own key, so your auditor doesn't have to take our word for it, and it streams to the SIEM you already run. How is Palma.ai deployed — SaaS, on-prem, VPC? Palma.ai is designed for enterprise environments: typically VPC or on-prem, including fully air-gapped, depending on your regulatory and security needs. The MCP layer and governance plane run on your infrastructure, so sensitive business data doesn't have to move into multi-tenant SaaS. We can also host it for you if you prefer. zh.summary: 在企业代理与工具之间统一管理 MCP、Skills、权限和审批。
zh.judgment: 价值在让已授权工作可靠通过，并使受限操作可追溯；不能只增加一道管理面板。
zh.replaces: 企业给不同助手分别配连接器、密钥和权限，审计时再拼各处日志。
zh.product: 官网说明一条连接路径覆盖工具和 Skills，核验身份、授权、参数策略和审批，并记录决策与成本。完整平台图需额外访问，本次没有取得后台或实测。
zh.customer: 企业 IT、安全和代理平台团队是明确使用者。买方需求来自多助手与多工具并存，员工仍希望工作顺畅，治理不能让每次任务变成重复申请。
zh.workflow: 用户的工具调用经过身份映射、工具包授权、参数检查和必要人工确认，再由受控凭据执行并记录。应核验拒绝理由、撤权时效与代理切换后的策略一致性。
zh.business_model: 本次未取得公开价格，企业合同与实施收费需确认。工具数量、组织结构和身份连接可能带来配置成本，订阅假设应扣除持续策略维护。
zh.traction: 官网有具体架构与操作示例，没有取得独立部署效果或续约数据。界面中的员工、成本和审批记录是示例，不能当作生产交易规模。
zh.moat: 跨代理一致策略、凭据代理与审计可能形成集成优势。身份平台、API 网关和助手原生治理都能覆盖部分需求，差异应在真正的参数与工作流约束。
zh.funding_read: 资金支持企业交付，但采购价值需要落在已批准任务完成和可查责任。下一里程碑是多工具实际部署，而不是宣传兼容的助手名单。
zh.risks: 策略错误可能阻断正常工作或放行越权，凭据映射失误可能扩大影响。新工具与 Skill 更新也会增加规则维护负担。
zh.takeaway: 把治理放在实际工具调用和工作参数上。给被拒任务可理解的理由与申请路径，同时让正常任务保持短流程。
zh.watch_next: 看错误拒绝、越权拦截、审批等待和撤权生效时间。记录新增工具的配置工时及组织范围扩张后的支持成本。

en.summary: Enterprise governance of MCP tools, Skills, permissions and approvals across assistants.
en.judgment: Authorized work should flow reliably while restricted actions remain traceable.
en.replaces: Configuring connectors, credentials and permissions separately, then reconstructing audit trails.
en.product: The site describes a shared connector checking identity, access, arguments and approvals, with decision and cost records. The full platform map is gated; no backend or live execution was tested.
en.customer: IT, security and agent-platform teams are stated users. Multiple tools create demand, while employees need usable work paths rather than repeated access requests.
en.workflow: Tool calls pass identity mapping, entitlement, argument checks and approval, then use brokered credentials and logs. Denials, revocation and consistency across assistants require verification.
en.business_model: Public prices were unavailable. Enterprise and implementation terms need confirmation; tools and identity structures create configuration and policy-upkeep costs.
en.traction: Architecture and examples were reviewed without independent deployment or renewal evidence. Illustrated employees, costs and approvals are not production scale.
en.moat: Consistent policy, credential brokerage and audit integration may differentiate it. Identity platforms, gateways and native assistant controls compete on real workflow constraints.
en.funding_read: Capital supports enterprise delivery, measured through completed authorized tasks and clear accountability. Actual multi-tool deployment matters more than a compatibility list.
en.risks: Wrong policies can block work or allow excess access, while mapping errors widen impact. Tool and Skill updates create ongoing rule maintenance.
en.takeaway: Govern actual tool arguments and actions. Give denied tasks understandable reasons and a request path while keeping routine work short.
en.watch_next: Watch false denials, excess-access prevention, approval time and revocation latency, plus configuration and support effort as scope grows.
